fields.hero_description: Build a botox consent form with your medical director's wording, an e-signature, and every signed copy in a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Each Signed Botox Consent Form Holds
fields.features_subheading: Your medical director owns the clinical wording. The form collects the answers and the signature on one patient record.
fields.feature_1:
Your medical director's health questions

Turn each health question your medical director writes into a yes or no field with a box for details. Any yes moves to the top of the record, where the injector reads it first.
fields.feature_2:
Consent statements initialed one at a time

Break the consent wording into short statements, and the patient initials each one. The wording carries a version number, which shows the exact text each patient agreed to and when.
fields.feature_3:
An e-signature on the patient's phone

A patient can sign on their own phone the night before or on the tablet at your front desk. The app captures each e-signature and keeps it with the answers and wording it confirms.
fields.feature_4:
Photo consent asked as its own question

Ask about before and after photos separately: chart only, or chart and marketing. The answer is saved with every photo on the record, and marketing pulls only photos marked for it.
fields.feature_5:
The treatment details on the same row

After the visit, the injector adds the areas treated, the product, and the lot number to the row that already holds the signed consent. That row sits in a database you own.
fields.feature_6:
Source code your developer can take over

On paid plans, export the full source to your GitHub repository when the form needs to live inside your practice website. Your developer can then host it on your own servers.

fields.usecase_heading: How Med Spas Use a Botox Consent Form
fields.tab_content_1:
One record for the consent and the lot number

Sabine Harker books forehead lines and crow's feet at Saffron Hill Aesthetics and e-signs her consent the night before. After the treatment, injector Pilar Esquivel adds the product, lot C4471C3, and the 2 areas treated to the same record. A later search for that lot lists every patient treated from it.
fields.tab_content_2:
For chart-only photos, no place in the gallery

Mallow Street Skin Studio asks every patient how their photos may be used. Wynne Talcott picks chart only. Her 4 photos from Thursday are saved to her record and tagged chart only. The studio's marketing team works from a gallery that lists only photos tagged for marketing, and Wynne's are not in it.
fields.tab_content_3:
Each yes goes to Dr. Esterly before the visit

Every patient at Cordova Skin Clinic answers the health questions written by its medical director, Dr. Theo Esterly. Lisette Hartwell fills in her form on Sunday and answers yes to the medicines question. Dr. Esterly gets an email with her answer at the top, 2 days before her Tuesday appointment.
fields.tab_content_4:
After version 4, every returning patient signs again

Fairhollow Aesthetics changed its consent wording this month, and version 4 replaced version 3. The 38 returning patients who signed version 3 get the new wording with their next booking reminder. So far 14 have signed and 24 have not. Maren Kolb signs from her reminder link, and version 3 stays on her record.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Botox Consent Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to create a botox consent form your medical director approves and patients e-sign before the visit.
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Decide how photos may be used
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down each treatment area you book, such as frown lines, forehead lines, and crow's feet, plus any filler done at the same visit. Each becomes a choice at the top of the form, and the sections a patient sees follow from it.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Ask your medical director to write or approve every health question, starting from the ones on your current paper form. Give each question a yes or no answer and a box for details, and put any question the director adds at the end.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Have your medical director and a healthcare attorney review the consent statements before the form goes live. Number that wording as version 1 and note the date. Each later change gets the next number, and returning patients sign it.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Decide what patients can choose for before and after photos, such as keeping them in the chart or also allowing marketing use. Ask it as its own question, apart from the treatment consent, and agree with your marketing team which tag lets them use a photo.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Paste your health questions, consent statements, and photo choices into one prompt. Emergent builds a form and a patient table to match. To change a question or add a filler section later, describe the change in a new prompt.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Connect it to your booking software
fields.howto_step_6_des: Link each signed record to its appointment in the booking software you already use, since the app can connect to any tool with an API. Send the form link with every booking confirmation, and keep a tablet at the front desk for walk-ins.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Test it as two different patients
fields.howto_step_7_des: Fill in the form twice yourself, once as a new patient who answers yes to a health question and once as a returning patient on the old wording. Check that the medical director gets the email and the new version appears, then open both records.

faq_plan.q: What is a botox consent form?
faq_plan.a: A botox consent form is the document a patient reads and signs before a Botox treatment. It holds the patient's answers to the practice's health questions, the areas to be treated, and the consent statements the medical director approved, with the patient's signature and the date.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a botox consent form?
faq_plan.a: Collect your health questions and the consent wording your medical director approved, then describe the form in plain English to Emergent's AI form builder. Emergent builds a working form, with a table of signed records, from that description. To add a photo consent or a filler section later, prompt again.

faq_plan.q: Can a filler consent form and a botox consent form be one document?
faq_plan.a: Yes, if your medical director agrees. Give the toxin and the filler their own sections, each with its own consent statements and signature line. A patient who gets toxin only that day signs only that section, and a patient who gets both signs twice on one record.

faq_plan.q: How should a botox consent form handle before and after photos?
faq_plan.a: Ask about photos as a question of their own, apart from the treatment consent, with a choice between keeping them in the chart and allowing marketing use. Let the patient change that answer later, and record the date of each change. A tattoo consent form can use the same split when an artist wants to post finished work.

faq_plan.q: What health questions should a botox consent form ask?
faq_plan.a: Your medical director decides. The FDA-approved Medication Guide for Botox and Botox Cosmetic tells patients to tell their doctor about all their medical conditions and all the medicines they take. Those two topics make a fair starting list for the director to review and expand.

faq_plan.q: Should a botox consent form record the product and lot number?
faq_plan.a: Yes, if you want each treatment traceable to its signed consent. The FDA-approved Medication Guide tells patients who have had other botulinum toxin injections to be sure their doctor knows exactly which product they received. A product and lot field, filled in by the injector, lets your practice tell a patient exactly what they received.

faq_plan.q: How often should returning patients re-sign a botox consent form?
faq_plan.a: Set the rule with your medical director. One approach is to have patients confirm their health answers at every visit and sign again whenever the consent wording changes. The same rule suits a permanent makeup consent form, where touch-up visits come back to the same wording.

faq_plan.q: Can patients e-sign a botox consent form on their phone before the appointment?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Send the form link with the booking confirmation, and the patient signs on any phone before arriving. With Emergent, each signed form is saved to a database you own. Ask your healthcare attorney what your practice needs for consent signed electronically.

faq_plan.q: Is there a free way to build a botox consent form online?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Emergent is free to start, and the free tier covers building and publishing a botox consent form. The form has no response caps, however many patients book and sign it.

faq_plan.q: Can I send a health history and a botox consent form in one link?
faq_plan.a: Yes, if your medical director wants them together. Put the health history first and the consent form second, each as its own section with its own heading. The patient answers both in one sitting, and the history and the signature land on one record.

plan.angle: The top 10 is ten clinic and hospital PDFs, each one static sheet a patient prints and signs once, with no record behind it. This page names what a botox consent form records and shows the four places a med spa needs more than paper: the signed consent and the injector's treatment record (areas, product, lot number) on one row, a photo consent that keeps chart-only photos out of marketing, a yes on the health questions reaching the medical director before the visit, and returning patients signing again when the medical director changes the consent wording. Medical content stays with the practice: the page never states risks, eligibility or who may inject, and quotes the FDA Medication Guide only for what it asks patients to tell their doctor.
